explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Formula.** Use the Combined Gas Law: $$ \frac{P_1 V_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2 V_2}{T_2} $$.
**Step 2: Substitution.** Let the new conditions be $$ P_2 = 2P_1 $$ and $$ T_2 = 2T_1 $$.
**Step 3: Solve for $$ V_2 $$.**
$$ V_2 = V_1 \cdot \left(\frac{P_1}{P_2}\right) \cdot \left(\frac{T_2}{T_1}\right) $$
$$ V_2 = V_1 \cdot \left(\frac{P_1}{2P_1}\right) \cdot \left(\frac{2T_1}{T_1}\right) $$
$$ V_2 = V_1 \cdot \left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \cdot 2 = V_1 $$.
**Conclusion:** The volume remains the same.

similar_questions.stem: Commercial HCl is 36% by mass of hydrogen chloride and has a density of 1.18 g/mL. Determine the molality and molarity of the solution? (Molar mass of HCl = 36.5 g/mol).
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Find Molarity (M).**
Assume 1 L (1000 mL) of solution.
Mass of solution = $$ Density \times Volume = 1.18 \, g/mL \times 1000 \, mL = 1180 \, g $$.
Mass of HCl = $$ 36\% \text{ of } 1180 \, g = 0.36 \times 1180 = 424.8 \, g $$.
Moles of HCl = $$ \frac{Mass}{Molar \, Mass} = \frac{424.8 \, g}{36.5 \, g/mol} \approx 11.64 \, mol $$.
Molarity (M) = $$ \frac{11.64 \, mol}{1 \, L} = 11.64 \, M $$.

**Step 2: Find Molality (m).**
Mass of solvent (water) = $$ Total \, mass - HCl \, mass = 1180 \, g - 424.8 \, g = 755.2 \, g = 0.7552 \, kg $$.
Molality (m) = $$ \frac{Moles \, of \, solute}{Mass \, of \, solvent \, (kg)} = \frac{11.64 \, mol}{0.7552 \, kg} \approx 15.41 \, m $$.
